Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday directed that testing for Influenza-A (H1N1) be provided free of cost at all government health facilities in the state, and ordered stronger surveillance and treatment arrangements in districts reporting higher cases.Reviewing the state's Influenza-A and seasonal influenza situation, Adityanath also directed private healthcare institutions not to charge more than the prescribed fee for H1N1 tests, and asked hospitals to ensure adequate medicines, testing and isolation facilities and prepare separate ICU wards for serious patients, according to an official statement.

Advt

He also ordered detailed guidelines on H1N1 prevention and treatment, effective teleconsultation services and intensified screening with the help of ANMs, ASHA workers and other health personnel to identify suspected cases, it stated.Experts informed the meeting that 685 laboratory-confirmed H1N1 cases had been reported in the state as of Wednesday. The infection, a type of Influenza-A virus, spreads mainly through droplets released while coughing or sneezing. Symptoms include fever, runny nose, cough, sore throat, headache, body ache, chills and red eyes, it added.

"Ensure timely identification and treatment of patients. Wherever cases are increasing, surveillance should be strengthened and necessary medical arrangements made immediately," the chief minister said.

He directed that patients with mild symptoms be advised home rest and self-isolation according to medical advice, while serious cases should receive immediate treatment. Special attention should be given to children, pregnant women, people above 65 and those with serious pre-existing illnesses.

Hospitals were asked to have separate counters for patients with influenza-like symptoms and ensure a referral system based on the patient's condition so that serious cases receive timely treatment without unnecessarily burdening hospitals.Experts said breathing difficulty, chest pain, extreme drowsiness, low blood pressure, blood-stained sputum and bluish nails could indicate severe illness. In children, persistent high fever, inability to eat, seizures, rapid or difficult breathing and worsening of an existing illness were listed as warning signs.

Advt

The government said adequate stocks of oseltamivir capsules and syrup and H1N1 vaccine were available. District hospitals have flu help desks, sample collection facilities and separate flu OPDs, while medical colleges have testing facilities, medicines and isolation beds, with adequate RT-PCR kits.Adityanath directed officials to strengthen public awareness and provide simple, accurate information on what people should and should not do.

"Ensure that there is no unnecessary panic," he said, stressing hand hygiene, cough and sneeze precautions and other infection-prevention measures at hospitals and crowded places.

Advt

He directed continuous monitoring of the situation and immediate action in districts witnessing a rise in cases.
